There are
four things I would implement alongside this document
, because they materially improve the protection rather than just adding legal language:
1. At signup, use an
unchecked checkbox

saying: “I agree to the Terms of Service and acknowledge the Privacy Policy.” Store the user ID/email, timestamp, Terms version, and ideally the exact version of the Terms they accepted. 2. Make permissions technically read-only wherever possible. The legal Terms saying “read-oriented” are much less useful if Convalesce actually receives broad administrative credentials. 3. Keep a
kill switch

so you can immediately revoke a user's access and disable integrations if you detect abuse, unusual cost, compromised credentials, or security testing. 4. Once the Delaware C-Corp exists, update the Terms so the corporation becomes the provider and execute separate
founder IP assignment agreements
transferring the relevant Convalesce IP from Samarth and Vedanshu to the company. The “Future Incorporation” section helps with continuity, but it does not replace the actual corporate/IP paperwork.
